$comment: The structured, machine-readable comment block scripts/land-stack.mjs
reads to decide whether a tier-1 pull request (governance/review-tiers.json)
carries two independent reviews (#1187 comment 5800142871). Defined here
once, per the task's own instruction, rather than as a second undocumented
grammar living only inside land-stack.mjs.
WHY A COMMENT BLOCK, NOT A NATIVE GITHUB REVIEW: every agent session in
this repository authenticates as the same GitHub account (the owner's --
see docs/HITL.md, 'Honour-system limits'). GitHub itself refuses to let
one account both open and formally review-approve the same pull request,
so the native review feature cannot even be used for a second opinion
here, and scripts/collect-review-evidence.mjs's own `instanceId: login`
choice (packages/controller/src/review/github.ts) cannot distinguish one
session from another on one account either. A structured comment,
carrying its own caller-assigned `instanceId`, is the only way this
repository can express 'two distinct sessions reviewed this' at all.
REUSES packages/controller/src/review/types.ts's ReviewRecord SHAPE
(reviewerId, instanceId, provider, submittedAt, state, depth, headSha) as
its base, per the task instruction to reuse that schema's shape rather
than invent an unrelated one -- without importing or modifying that
package (SCOPE: scripts and governance only, no packages/* changes this
slice). Extended with `role`, `model`, `effort` and `class`: fields
ReviewRecord's v3 shape does not carry, because native GitHub review
evidence never needed them. A future slice may fold these into a real
packages/controller schema bump (the Fable second opinion's REVIEW_
EVIDENCE_VERSION 4 proposal); this slice keeps that package untouched and
expresses the superset here instead.
HOW IT IS POSTED: a plain PR comment whose body contains a block of the
form below. A comment MAY carry more than one block (`scripts/land-stack.mjs`'s
`parseReviewRecordComments` extracts every match in a `while` loop, not
just the first) -- an earlier draft of this document said 'exactly one
block', which the parser has never actually enforced. The HTML-comment
wrapper keeps it invisible in rendered Markdown, the same convention
this repository's own automated reviewer already uses for its own
machine-readable metadata.
<!-- foundry-review-record
{ "schemaVersion": 1, "role": "reviewer", ... }
NOT RECOGNIZED INSIDE A QUOTE, FENCE, OR INDENTED CODE BLOCK (#1187
review round 4, blocking finding 2): before scanning for the marker,
`stripQuotedAndFencedContent` removes every triple-backtick/tilde fenced
code block, inline code span (single or double backticks), blockquoted
line, and classic 4-space/tab-indented code block from the comment body.
A comment that merely QUOTES or ILLUSTRATES the marker syntax -- for
example a review comment discussing this repository's own convention,
or this very contract's own example above once rendered inside a code
fence -- produces no record at all, real or malformed: it is invisible
to this module entirely, not merely rejected. The load-bearing
convention is a BARE block directly in the comment body, never fenced,
quoted, or indented.
AUTHORIZATION (#1187 review round 4, blocking finding 2, first part):
a block counts toward tier-1 independence ONLY when the posting
account's collaborator permission on this repository, checked live via
`repos/{owner}/{repo}/collaborators/{username}/permission`, is `admin`
or `write`. This repository is public; without this check, a block from
any GitHub account with no relationship to it at all satisfied tier-1.
A permission of `read`/`none`, or a login this module could not
resolve, makes the record `_authorization: "unauthorized"` -- it can
never count toward an approval, AND (see 'A REJECT IS STICKY' below) it
can never count toward a rejection either, or a stranger could
permanently deny every pull request by posting one comment. A FAILED
permission lookup (the API call itself errored, a genuinely different
outcome from a confirmed 'no') is `_authorization: "unknown"` and
refuses the whole gate outright -- see 'REFUSING THE GATE' below --
rather than being silently read either as authorized or as
unauthorized.
STALENESS: a record's `headSha` must equal the pull request's live head
at merge time or it is not treated as current evidence -- never
downgraded, never partially trusted. Among records that remain, the
LATEST wins per (role, instanceId) pair, ordered by the COMMENT'S OWN
`created_at` (GitHub-assigned, never editable by the poster), NOT by
the record's self-declared `submittedAt` -- an earlier draft of this
document, and of `scripts/land-stack.mjs` itself, ordered by
`submittedAt`, which a poster could backdate or postdate to win or lose
a supersession race on purpose (#1187 review at df15ab87,
should-fix). `submittedAt` remains a required field (the record's own
claim about when it was decided) but no longer decides ordering.
REFUSING THE GATE, NOT SILENTLY DROPPING (#1187 review at df15ab87,
blocking finding 3; tightened at #1187 review round 4): an AUTHORIZED
comment that is unparseable JSON, or was EDITED after posting (its
`updated_at` differs from its `created_at`) and claims the pull
request's exact current head, refuses the WHOLE tier-1 gate outright --
it is not simply dropped and worked around by other, untouched
comments. An UNAUTHORIZED comment is never suspicious this way,
whatever it contains: only a confirmed collaborator's tampered or
garbled evidence is worth refusing the gate over.
A REJECT IS STICKY (#1187 review round 4, blocking finding 3): an
authorized `reject`/`changes-requested` record at the current head
blocks the merge regardless of what else is wrong with it -- missing
`depth`/`model`, an unparseable `submittedAt`, anything -- and cannot
be superseded by ANY later record, from the same `instanceId` or
otherwise, whatever that later record's self-declared `submittedAt`
claims. `state` is matched case-insensitively (`"Reject"` counts the
same as `"reject"`), and `headSha` is matched leniently for this
purpose only: case-insensitively, and an unambiguous 7-or-more-character
prefix of the live head counts as current (a hand-typed short SHA is
still current evidence). A reject with NO `headSha` at all cannot be
placed at any head, current or stale, so it ALSO refuses the gate
outright rather than being silently un-matched. The only way to clear a
sticky rejection is a genuinely new head whose commit changes at least
one file (a no-op commit does not count -- #1187 review round 4,
should-fix) -- there is no decision-record override path in this
slice.
rule: One block, one record. `schemaVersion` must be exactly 1. `role` is
`"author"` or `"reviewer"` and selects which required-field set below
applies. `reviewerId` is the provider-neutral, opaque identity that
posted the comment (the same GitHub login for every role in this
repository today -- see the header comment above); it is descriptive
only and never used to establish independence. `instanceId` is
caller-assigned, opaque, and is the field independence is actually
computed on: stable for one session, distinct across sessions, per
packages/controller/src/review/types.ts's own `ReviewRecord.instanceId`
contract. `provider` and `model` are free-form opaque strings (no vendor
enum, matching ReviewRecord's own `provider` doc comment) -- e.g.
provider `"anthropic"`, model `"claude-opus-4-1"`. `effort` is a
free-form string (e.g. `"high"`) and is informational only in this
slice. `class` is one of `C1`/`C2`/`C3` (governance/model-qualifications/
allowlist.json). NEITHER `class` NOR `effort` IS READ OR ENFORCED BY
land-stack.mjs AT ALL IN THIS SLICE -- an earlier draft of this file
claimed land-stack reports on `class` once the allowlist is approved;
#1187 review at 8e6d97ea (should-fix 12) found no such code existed.
Reading and reporting model qualification is real, separate work left to
a later slice; these two fields are carried on the schema now so a
future slice does not need a second schema bump to add them.
A `role: "author"` record declares the PR author's own session identity;
its `state` is always the literal string `"declared"` and it carries no
`depth` or `model` (an author is not reviewing). EXACTLY ONE current
(non-stale, non-edited) author record must exist for tier-1 independence
to be satisfiable: land-stack treats both its absence AND more than one
such record as a failed check -- a second author-role record is never
silently resolved to "the first one found", which would otherwise let a
reviewer declare itself the author to dodge the independence check
(#1187 review at 8e6d97ea, should-fix 9).
A `role: "reviewer"` record's `state` is one of `approved`,
`changes-requested`, `reject`, or `commented`; `depth` is `primary` for
an ordinary single-pass review or `secondary` for a deliberate second,
independent pass (mirrors ReviewDepth's own contract; this schema does
not currently define `secondary-incomplete`, since a comment either
exists or does not).
`headSha` (all roles) must be the 40-character lowercase hex commit SHA
this record was written against. `patchId` is optional free-form data,
kept for parity with ReviewEvidenceBundle's own optional `patchId` and
not yet validated by land-stack in this slice.
Tier-1 independence (governance/review-tiers.json's `tier1.review`) is
satisfied only when, among current (non-stale, non-edited) records at
the pull request's live head: exactly one author record exists; ANY
independent reviewer record (instanceId distinct from the author's)
whose `state` is `reject` or `changes-requested` refuses the merge
immediately and is NEVER outvoted by a later clean pair from other
reviewers (#1187 review at 8e6d97ea, blocking finding 1 -- matches the
decision-tier rule's own "a reject is never outvoted"); otherwise, at
least two independent reviewer records must both have `state`
`"approved"` (`"commented"` never counts, per blocking finding 2),
distinct `instanceId` from each other, one `depth: "primary"` and the
other `depth: "secondary"` (two records at the same depth never pair,
matching the decision-tier rule's own "a first reviewer plus a
stronger-model second opinion"), and differ in `model` OR `provider`.
A reviewer record whose `instanceId` equals the author's is excluded
from consideration entirely -- it is evidence of the same session
reviewing its own change, not a second opinion.
